qeb5df016.question: Item f2: architectureShape names the definitions file, validator, registry, provider factory, CLI provider and clients by role rather than quoting each s1 bundle path inline (partial).

summary.prose: Each new runner is a new model family in insrc's shipped model definitions: one for the Claude command-line tool on Ollama and one for the Codex command-line tool on Ollama. Each declares that its tool runs on Ollama, and each of its models is marked cloud or local. A tier selects one of these families exactly as it selects a family today. The daemon starts the same command-line tool it starts today, pointed at Ollama for that run only, and the three settings clients list the new families from the definitions answer they already read.

body.frameworkSummary: Model the two new runners as two new families in the model definitions (alternative a1). The definitions file, its validator and the definitions answer gain two families, 'ollama-claude' and 'ollama-codex', each with the CLI kind of the tool it runs and a host mark 'ollama'; every model of those families carries a hosting mark, 'cloud' or 'local'. Tier settings, effort filtering and provider construction keep their one per-family path. A family with the Ollama host mark builds the existing CLI provider with an Ollama target applied to that subprocess only, and clients use the host mark to show cloud/local and to never offer unlisted model ids for those families.
body.architectureShape: Three layers, each changed in one place. (1) Definitions layer (s1): the shipped definitions file and the catalog validator admit a five-member closed family set; the two new families carry cliKind and host 'ollama', have no tier defaults or summariser of their own, and every model carries hosting. The registry exposes host and hosting, resolves a tier on a host family only to a declared model (otherwise a 'model-not-supported' resolution), maps a CLI client to its direct family only, and refuses the unknown-model check and the approved-model store for host families. The definitions answer gains the two marks. (2) Run layer (s2): the per-family provider factory passes the family's host to the CLI provider; for host 'ollama' the provider starts the claude CLI with an environment pointing it at the local Ollama (base URL, placeholder token, empty API key) or the codex CLI with Ollama's local-provider flags, adds nothing for direct families, checks Ollama reachability and the model's availability before a run and names the cause on failure, and keeps calls serial. (3) Client layer (s3, s4, s5): the terminal UI, the VS Code picker and settings, and the JetBrains Settings page list the new families from the answer, label each model cloud or local, offer effort only from the model's efforts, withhold 'Enter another model id' for host families, and show the tier the daemon reports. The on-disk tier validator (isRunner, src/config/analyze.ts:371) checks family ids against the list derived from the shipped definitions file (src/config/model-defaults.ts:57-60), so it admits the two new families with no code change; s1 covers it with a regression test. Classification rule (s1): today the daemon decides family behaviour from two tests that the new families would pass the wrong way, 'the family is not ollama' and 'the family has a CLI kind'. s1 classifies every such site into one of two meanings and keys it accordingly: 'runs a CLI' stays on the CLI kind and includes the host families (provider kind in src/analyze/context/shaper-provider.ts:228, :274, :287, :339; src/analyze/context/driver.ts:1160; src/daemon/list-models.ts:92-105; src/daemon/model-definitions.ts:104, :203), while 'a vendor CLI family' keys on the host mark being absent and excludes the host families: tier defaults and summariser required by the validator (isCliFamily, src/daemon/model-catalog.ts:140-142, :186-191), the unknown-model check (src/daemon/model-check.ts:319-320), the approved-model store (src/daemon/model-registry.ts:142, already closed), the unlisted-model fallback (src/daemon/model-registry.ts:277-278), the tier write's model check (src/daemon/config-write.ts:74) and run attribution by CLI-kind label prefix (src/workflow/attribution.ts:49), which must name the family that ran, not the first family with that CLI kind. The validator's test fixtures (src/daemon/__tests__/model-catalog.test.ts:35) grow to the five-family set.

sharedContracts.name: Ollama-hosted CLI families in the definitions answer
sharedContracts.purpose: The wire shape every consumer reads to know the two new families, that they run a CLI on Ollama, and which of their models are cloud or local.

sharedContracts.name: Tier resolution on an Ollama-hosted family
sharedContracts.purpose: How the daemon reports the tier it actually runs when the tier names a host family, including a model the definitions do not declare, so the run layer and every settings surface show the same outcome.

storyBoundaries.internal: The shipped definitions entries for the two families and their models (which cloud and local models are supported), the catalog validator's five-member check and the 'hosting required on host families' rule, the registry's mapping from a CLI client to its direct family only, and the refusal of the unknown-model check and the approved-model store for host families stay inside s1.

How the CLI provider points a run at Ollama (the claude environment and the codex local-provider flags, applied only to that subprocess), the pre-run checks that Ollama answers and the model is available or signed in for a cloud model, the failure messages that name the cause, and the time limit that keeps a run from waiting forever stay inside s2.
The terminal UI's runner list, model list with cloud/local labels, effort step and the withheld 'enter another id' path for host families, and its display of the resolved tier, stay inside s3.

The VS Code tier picker's family and model steps, the settings write validation that refuses an undeclared model for a host family, the cloud/local labels and the withheld 'enter another id' item stay inside s4.
The JetBrains Settings page's family and model selectors, the cloud/local labels, the filter that keeps host families out of the model-check flow, and its display of the resolved tier stay inside s5.

nonFunctional.performance: No added cost on today's runners. A run on a host family adds one Ollama reachability and model-availability check before the CLI starts; a run never waits beyond the existing CLI time limit.
nonFunctional.security: The Ollama settings are applied only to the started subprocess's environment or arguments; the user's own CLI configuration files and the daemon's environment are never changed. No API key is stored; the claude CLI gets the placeholder token Ollama accepts locally.
nonFunctional.observability: The daemon logs the family, model, hosting and Ollama target of each host-family run, and a failed pre-run check logs which check failed; the tier resolution reported to clients names a 'model-not-supported' fallback.
nonFunctional.durability: Nothing new is persisted: tier settings keep their stored shape, and the new families live in the shipped definitions file.

phases.name: Phase A — definitions contract
phases.rationale: s1 owns both shared contracts (sc1, sc2); every other Story consumes them.
phases.backwardCompat: The three existing families keep their entries, ids, tier defaults and resolution; a client that does not yet understand the host and hosting marks still reads the answer, because the marks are additive.

phases.name: Phase B — run on Ollama and expose in settings
phases.rationale: Each depends only on s1 and on sc1/sc2, so the daemon run path and the three client surfaces can land in any order after Phase A.
phases.backwardCompat: Direct-family runs start the CLI exactly as before (no Ollama environment or flags); clients keep their current behaviour for the three existing families, including 'Enter another model id' for the direct CLI families.

rolloutOverview.orderingRationale: s1 is the only Story every other Story depends on and the owner of both shared contracts, so it lands first; s2-s5 have no edges between them and each consumes only sc1/sc2.

riskyBits.area: Clients exposing the new families before the daemon can run them
riskyBits.why: If a client ships s3/s4/s5 before s2, a user could pick a host family the daemon cannot yet run.
riskyBits.mitigation: The daemon only lists the new families once s1 lands, and s2's pre-run check reports a clear cause; release the daemon with s2 before announcing the client releases.

riskyBits.why: Two families now share each CLI kind; code that maps a CLI kind back to a family could pick the Ollama family and change today's behaviour (k6).
riskyBits.mitigation: s1 restricts the client-to-family mapping to direct families and adds a regression test that today's mapping is unchanged.

riskyBits.why: Ollama's cloud model names change; a shipped entry may stop existing.
riskyBits.mitigation: s2's pre-run check names a missing model as the cause; the list is data in the shipped definitions file and is updated with a daemon release.

alternativesConsidered.name: Two new model families in the definitions
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add a Claude-on-Ollama family and a Codex-on-Ollama family to the shipped definitions, each marked as running its CLI on Ollama, with every model marked cloud or local.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
The definitions file and its validator gain two families next to the three existing ones. Each new family names the CLI it runs (the same claude/codex kind the existing CLI families carry) and additionally declares that the CLI is pointed at Ollama; each of its models carries the existing fields (id, display name, efforts, input limit) plus a hosting mark, cloud or local. The family set becomes five, still a closed list validated at load, and a tier selects one of the new families exactly as it selects a family today, so the tier, model and effort settings are reused unchanged.

The daemon turns a tier on a new family into the same CLI provider it builds for the existing CLI families, with one extra input: the Ollama endpoint that this run's CLI process is pointed at (an environment for the claude CLI, flags for the codex CLI), applied only to that subprocess. The definitions answer the clients already read carries the new families and the two new marks, so each client lists them through the code path it already has; each client uses the 'runs on Ollama' mark to show cloud/local and to withhold the 'enter another model id' path for those families.
pros: Follows the per-family definitions shape Epic ce99b720 established: a runner is a family, so tier resolution, effort filtering and provider construction keep one code path.
The three clients already iterate the answer's families, so a new family appears in every surface without a new endpoint; the client change is limited to reading two new marks.
Today's three families keep their file entries, ids and settings byte for byte, which keeps k6 checkable by an unchanged-definitions test.
cons: The closed family-id union and the 'exactly one entry per family' validation grow from three to five members, touching every exhaustive switch over family ids.
Two families share a CLI kind with an existing family, so every place that maps a CLI kind back to a family (the client-to-family mapping) must pick the direct one, not the Ollama one.
Clients that today equate 'has a CLI kind' with 'accepts unlisted model ids' must change that rule, in three codebases.

alternativesConsidered.name: Ollama as a transport on the existing CLI families
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep the two CLI families and add an 'on Ollama' transport choice to the tier setting, with each CLI family declaring a separate list of Ollama-served models.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
The definitions keep three families. Each CLI family gains a second model list, the Ollama-served models its CLI can run, each marked cloud or local. A tier setting gains a transport field (the CLI's own service, or Ollama); the model is validated against the list that matches the transport.

The daemon builds the same CLI provider for either transport, adding the Ollama endpoint to the subprocess when the tier's transport is Ollama. Clients add a transport selector to the tier editor and switch the model list on it.
pros: The family-id union and the client-to-family mapping stay unchanged.
A user sees the Claude tool as one runner with two hosting choices, which matches how the CLI vendors describe it.
cons: Changes the stored tier setting shape (a new field) in every client's write path and in the daemon's tier parser, which puts today's settings (k6) at risk and needs a migration story for tiers without the field.
Two model lists per family break the one-list-per-family invariant every client and the effort filter rely on today.
The 'enter another model id' rule now depends on transport as well as family, a two-variable condition in three codebases.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Scores 'partial' on k3 and k6: it adds a transport field to the stored tier setting and needs a default rule for every existing tier, so today's settings shape changes.

alternativesConsidered.name: CLI front-ends on the Ollama family
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep the Ollama family as the runner and let each of its models declare which CLI front-ends (claude, codex) may drive it.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
The Ollama family's model list is extended with cloud models and a hosting mark; each model lists the CLI front-ends that can drive it. A tier on the Ollama family gains an optional front-end choice; with none it calls Ollama directly as today, with one it starts that CLI pointed at Ollama.

The daemon branches on the front-end inside the Ollama provider path; clients add a front-end selector under the Ollama family.
pros: One model list for everything served by Ollama, so a model is declared once even if both CLIs can drive it.
cons: Mixes a direct-API runner and two subprocess runners inside one family, so the family no longer tells the daemon which provider kind to build; the provider choice depends on a per-tier field instead.
Cloud models would appear under the plain Ollama runner too unless separately excluded, contradicting the user decision that the plain runner stays as it is (k6).
Adds a tier field like a2, with the same migration and k6 exposure.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates k6 (the plain Ollama family's model list and behaviour change) and is 'partial' on k1, k2 and k3: one family would build a direct Ollama provider or a CLI subprocess depending on a per-tier field.
